page.layout: One printed page with a decorative woodcut border; running head and page number at the top; text in one column of roman and italic type; catchword-like signature "C 2" at the foot of the text block. No notes in the margins (the left edge shows only show-through and the neighbouring page, which is left out).

p.i: (scilicet ex auro) nobis eadem re-ipsa exhibet. Nec longè ab eadem Palingenius in Capricorno ablu-dere videtur, lib.10. cum inquit:
Huncjuvenem Arcadium infidũ-nimiumq́, fugacem Prendite, & immersũ stygÿs occidite lymphis, & quesequuntur.

main_text.p: Sed de his plus satis. Haud enim scio an hûc sint referenda, quæ prodit Hohenheimerus Doctor ille Helvetius in libro Thesauri thesaurorum, ubi de mineralibus scribens Natura (inquit) progignit Minerale in visceribus terræ, cujus duo sunt genera, quæ in multis locis & finibus Europæ reperiuntur: Optimum autem in figura majoris Mundi est in ortu astri Sphæræ Solis. Alterum in astro Meridionali, quod est in primo flore suo, ab astro visci terræ productum

page.notes: The final line "ductum" is printed at the right of the last text line, and the first word of the next page is not visible. The italic "Huncjuvenem" is underlined in the print, and "Prendite" also carries an underline; the underlining is not reproduced. The paragraph ends mid-sentence at the foot, as printed, and continues on the next page. Some letters in the italic lines are uncertain (e.g. "stygÿs", "visci") and should be checked against the scan.
